title: The Environment is the only place tools execute
context: The AI SDK will happily execute tools itself if a tool is declared with an execute function. That would put tool execution inside the contestant, where the harness cannot observe it.
decision: Contestants return tool CALLS and never run them. Tools are declared without execute and the agent is capped at stepCountIs(1); the Environment executes every call.
consequences: ToolLoopAgent is used as a single-step agent. In exchange, DB hashing, Layer-1 event capture, and parity between a local model and a deployed HTTP endpoint are all possible.

title: Cache-first prompt layout: stable prefix first, variable content last
context: Prompt caching is a prefix match. One changed byte anywhere in the prefix invalidates everything after it. A benchmark running tens of thousands of conversations pays for that mistake on every call.
decision: Assemble every prompt stable-prefix-first: system/policy, tool schemas, docs, conversation so far, this turn. No timestamp, UUID, turn counter or session id ever goes in a system prompt.
consequences: Per-turn context must go in the message list, never interpolated into the system prompt. Prompt hashes are recorded in the manifest so a drift is detectable.

title: Split "can place a breakpoint" from "reports cache reads"
context: The cache probe gated on supportsExplicitCaching, using "can the caller place a breakpoint?" to answer "is caching measurable at all?". It therefore skipped every provider that caches automatically.
decision: Two flags. supportsExplicitCaching drives only whether providerOptions.anthropic.cacheControl is sent. reportsCacheReads drives whether the probe runs.
consequences: reportsCacheReads: false means unverified, not absent. --force-cache-check probes anyway; flip the flag once a real run reports.

title: OpenAI needs a stable promptCacheKey, or nothing caches
context: Four byte-identical 30,641-token OpenAI calls read zero cached tokens. The prefix layout was correct; the requests were being routed to different backends.
decision: Send a stable promptCacheKey for kind === openai, derived from the system-prompt hash and truncated to 64 chars, from one helper shared by the probe and the conversation paths.
consequences: Placement is automatic on OpenAI but routing is not. Without the key a sweep pays list price while believing the cache lever is engaged.

title: Do not send promptCacheOptions mode:explicit
context: The AI SDK exposes promptCacheOptions { mode: explicit } for OpenAI, which would make OpenAI caching deterministic like Anthropic. gpt-4.1-mini rejects it.
decision: Do not send prompt_cache_options. Re-check per model before assuming a newer contestant supports it.
consequences: OpenAI caching stays best-effort, so a miss there is INCONCLUSIVE rather than a proven defect. An SDK type surface is not proof a model accepts the field.

title: No provider honours seed; live reproducibility rests elsewhere
context: scenario.seed is passed on every call and recorded in the manifest, but Anthropic, OpenAI and Google all report seed as unsupported and sample freely.
decision: Keep passing and recording the seed, but never claim live runs are reproducible because of it. Reproducibility rests on pinned model version, prompt hashes, gold-DB hash and published transcripts.
consequences: Only the offline smoke is byte-reproducible. K (trials per scenario) is the real lever against variance, so per-scenario variance monitoring matters more, not less.

title: A gate check states only what it proves
context: pnpm smoke printed "G1 PASSED" after a run that makes zero model calls, but G1 has two clauses and the second requires a live call. Half a gate read as a whole one.
decision: Every gate check reports only the clause it actually exercised, and names the command that covers the rest. No check asserts a global gate state it cannot observe.
consequences: Output is wordier. In exchange a green check cannot be mistaken for a met gate.

title: Two decision logs, split by leakage risk
context: Decisions were accumulating in CLAUDE.md, which is a working guide that gets rewritten. A benchmark also cannot publish every decision it makes without leaking what it scores.
decision: Append-only ADR log in docs/decisions/ (public, committed) and docs/decisions-private/ (gitignored). Public ADRs may never cite private ones, in either direction of content or id.
consequences: Two places to look. CLAUDE.md becomes a guide that points at the log rather than a growing decision record.

title: Pin floating model aliases to dated snapshots
context: No provider honours seed (ADR-0006), so a silently repointed floating alias is the dominant remaining reproducibility risk: half a sweep could run against a different model with nothing in the manifest or the response to show it.
decision: Resolve floating aliases to dated snapshots at parseModelRef. Record both the snapshot and the requested ref in the manifest with a versionPinned flag. Pins are copied from the installed SDK model-id unions; an alias with no verified snapshot is left unpinned and warned about rather than guessed.
consequences: A result claiming reproducibility needs versionPinned true on every model; gemini-2.5-flash is currently the gap. MODEL_PINS goes stale like the price table and must be re-verified at freeze.
